frames.narration: Stage 1, pretraining. The data is raw text. At every position the model must guess the next token.
The model gives a probability to every possible next token.
The loss measures how little probability the real next token, 'mat', received. A low probability means a high loss.
Gradient descent moves every weight a small step that would have made 'mat' more likely. This repeats over a huge amount of text.
Stage 2, instruction tuning. The data is now requests with good answers, so the model learns to answer instead of continuing.
Stage 3, preference tuning. People pick the better of two answers, and the model is trained to prefer what they pick, with RLHF or DPO.
